title: Lua Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: print shows a value and moves to a new line.

entries.name: Keep a local value
entries.summary: local limits a name to its part of the program. This helps avoid accidental global names.
notes: Use local unless a name really needs to be global.

entries.name: Join text
entries.summary: Two dots join text in Lua. Joining text is called concatenation.

entries.name: Choose a message
entries.summary: if checks a condition. then starts its steps and end closes them.

example.code:
local score = 8
if score >= 5 then
 print("Pass")
else
 print("Try again")
end

entries.name: Use a table as a list
entries.summary: A table can act as an ordered list. The usual first position is 1.
notes: Index zero is not the first list item in ordinary Lua tables.

entries.name: Use named table fields
entries.summary: A table can also pair names with values. A dot reads a named field.

example.code:
local book = { title = "Moon Trip", pages = 24 }
print(book.title)

notes: A field that is not present gives nil.

entries.name: Count with a for loop
entries.summary: A numeric for loop includes both its start and end values.
notes: Use a comma between start and end, not a range operator.

entries.name: Visit list items
entries.summary: ipairs gives a position and value for list-style entries starting at 1.

example.code:
for _, pet in ipairs({"cat", "dog"}) do
 print(pet)
end

notes: ipairs stops at the first missing numbered value.

entries.name: Return a result
entries.summary: A function is a named group of steps. return sends a value back.

example.code:
local function twice(n)
 return n * 2
end
print(twice(4))

notes: Close the function with end before calling it.

entries.name: Use a fallback
entries.summary: nil means no value. or chooses the second value when the first is nil or false.
notes: Zero and empty strings are true values in Lua.

entries.name: Return two values
entries.summary: Lua functions can return several values. A matching assignment reads them.

example.code:
local function pair()
 return 3, 5
end
local a, b = pair()
print(a + b)

notes: One receiving variable keeps only the first returned value.

entries.name: Catch a failed call
entries.summary: pcall runs a function and reports whether it succeeded. The first result is true or false.

example.code:
local ok = pcall(function() error("Try again") end)
print(ok)

notes: The error message is a second result; the first result is the success flag.
